channel.title: GeoPulse. Geopolitics in brief
channel.description: Signal-first briefings on geopolitics, edited by Lavkesh Dwivedi.

item.title: Ebola en RDC, une épidémie hors de contrôle ?
item.description: Dans cet épisode d’Afrique 360°, Enrica Picco et Rinaldo Depagne reçoivent Frédéric Manantsoa Lai, coordinateur des urgences pour Médecins Sans Frontières, et Onesphore Sematumba, analyste senior pour la République démocratique du Congo et le Burundi à Crisis Group, pour parler de l’épidémie d’Ebola en RDC et de ses conséquences sur la population congolaise, déjà marquée par des années de conflit.

item.title: Avrupa Birliği ve Türkiye: Savunmada Birlik?
item.description: İkinci Dünya Savaşı sonrasında şekillenen uluslararası düzen giderek çözülürken, Ankara ve diğer Avrupa başkentlerindeki yetkililer güvenlik alanında birlikte hareket etmedikleri takdirde ciddi risklerle karşı karşıya kalacaklarının giderek daha fazla farkına varıyor. Tehdit algıları farklılık gösterse de, pragmatik ve esnek iş birliği yolları geliştirmeleri hâlâ mümkün. Avrupa Birliği ve Türkiye: Savunmada Birlik?

item.title: Nepal flood toll hits 389; rescue work in top gear
item.description: Government issues fresh flood alert after satellite imagery shows that a lake has formed upstream of Bhotekoshi River; “towns were wiped out in a span of a couple of hours,” says Foreign Minister Shishir Khamal At least 359 people dead in Nepal flood; rescue operations underway. At least 389 people dead in Nepal flood; rescue operations underway. Over 800 people rescued after the flash flood, 910 remain missing, say authorities; alert sounded along Bhotekoshi river as satellite images show blockage upstream; probe on to determine the role of glacial lakes in the devastating flood, says Nepal; 517 foreign nationals unaccounted for; Nepal PM Balendra Shah reaches nearest motorable town.

item.title: Trump Dismisses Fears of Russian Strike On NATO After CIA Chief Visits Moscow
item.description: US President Donald Trump told reporters that he does not believe Moscow will attack a NATO nation amid rising concerns that Russian President Vladimir Putin will strike a Baltic country or other member state to test the Western alliance’s resolve. Trump Dismisses Fears of Russian Strike On NATO After CIA Chief Visits Moscow.

item.title: Syria Kurdish women fighters discuss merger with interior ministry
item.description: The announcement came two days after the head of Kurdish fighters in Syria, Mazloum Abdi, announced the dissolution of the Syrian Democratic Forces (SDF). which includes the YPJ. under an agreement with Damascus Syria Kurdish women fighters discuss merger with interior ministry.

item.title: Why is Instagram’s design under fire in massive child safety case
item.description: Meta has agreed to a settlement worth up to $16.68 billion in a case alleging Facebook and Instagram were designed to keep children engaged and collect their data. The company denies wrongdoing, but the agreement could bring major changes for teenage users across the United States. Why is Instagram’s design under fire in massive child safety case.

item.title: Ukrainian Drone Spots SOS, Sparking 3-Day Rescue From Frontline Village
item.description: After a Ukrainian drone operator spotted an SOS sign outside a destroyed home in the Donetsk region, a three-day rescue mission was launched to save a couple who were the last remaining residents of their frontline village. Ukrainian Drone Spots SOS, Sparking 3-Day Rescue From Frontline Village.

item.title: Civilian risks grow as military activity continues, UN says
item.description: Damaged roads, disrupted services and ongoing military activity continue to put civilians at risk in south Lebanon as strikes between Israeli forces and Hezbollah continue, according to the UN’s peacekeeping mission in the country (UNIFIL). UN warns of growing civilian risks as military activity continues. Civilian risks grow as military activity continues, UN says.

item.title: Security Council LIVE: Tracking Syria’s transition
item.description: As Damascus continues to rebuild after more than a decade of war – from the recent dissolution of the Kurdish-led Syrian Democratic Forces to the United States’ removal of Syria from its sponsors of terrorism list – a top UN official warned the Security Council on Thursday that international support can help tackle outstanding challenges. item.title: Shock and devastation remain, a day after Himalayan flood disaster
item.description: Amid reports that hundreds of people are still missing in Nepal and China after a floodwater surge slammed into towns and villages on Wednesday, aid teams have been working to reach communities cut off by the disaster. Shock and devastation remain, a day after Himalayan flood disaster.

item.title: Latvia’s ‘Weekend Warriors’ Prepare For Potential Russian Threat
item.description: Latvia’s volunteer National Guard, the Zemessardze, has taken on a growing role in the country’s defense since Russia’s full-scale invasion of Ukraine. Following ordinary Latvians as they take part in military exercises, Current Time looks at why they give up their weekends to train. Latvia’s ‘Weekend Warriors’ Prepare For Potential Russian Threat.

item.title: Baltic States Arm For Russian Threat As Leaked Letter Shows Growing Fears
item.description: A letter seen by RFE/RL highlights mounting concern over Russian threats to the Baltic States. Latvia, Lithuania, and Estonia are boosting defenses and embracing new technology, but funding uncertainty, delayed projects, and gaps in capabilities raise questions about their readiness. Baltic States Arm For Russian Threat As Leaked Letter Shows Growing Fears.

item.title: Life-Saving Resource Or Political Weapon?
item.description: The Ibar River feeds Lake Gazivode, providing drinking water as well as water for crop irrigation and cooling power plants across Kosovo. But after recent local disputes, Serbian President Aleksandar Vucic has raised the prospect of altering the river's course upstream. Life-Saving Resource Or Political Weapon?

item.title: More health workers, stronger systems: Africa’s new ambitious goal
item.description: Facing a projected shortage of more than six million health professionals by 2035, African countries are stepping up efforts to strengthen their workforce, with a new decade-long plan announced on Wednesday during a meeting of health ministers in Addis Ababa, Ethiopia. More health workers, stronger systems: Africa’s new ambitious goal.

item.description: Paper products among hardest-hit sectors after trade negotiations broke down, with 25-50% tariffs estimatedAre you a Canadian boycotting US products?
